label: context.reference
text: Installing the lifecycle package connects no run. A lifecycle connection exists only after an operator or policy-granted worker authors an immutable lifecycle.connection payload, binds its exact artifact id with read access on every connected checkpoint of each emitter/handler-owner/agent-destination run, writes interface_state.<provider>.lifecycle_connection with the same connection id, exact system_lifecycle_events interface, and exact content-addressed ArtifactRef, grants only the destination interfaces/tools and lifecycle.decision.allowed outcome actually required, and authors the concrete run JSON interface bindings in canonical {interface,config:{artifact_policy:{mode,names,namespaces}}} form. The provider output checkpoint for lifecycle.event must leave through exact system_lifecycle_events; a sync event then derives its only lifecycle.decision return checkpoint on that same interface with verifier lifecycle_decision and mark lifecycle.decision.allowed. Handler results leave the executing provider through an explicit provider-to-system_lifecycle_events output checkpoint; an ordinary unverified lifecycle.decision input checkpoint is forbidden. Handler owners receive the exact event artifact before Command becomes a granted Tool route, MCP becomes an exact World-interface route, Prompt becomes an exact provider route, or Agent becomes an exact system_worker_* route. Agent additionally requires a connected destination run whose system_worker_* input checkpoint hands lifecycle.handler.task to its provider and whose provider result checkpoint emits lifecycle.decision or lifecycle.handler.output back to system_lifecycle_events. Every edited run/policy record and the connection payload is content-addressed in lifecycle.connection.authoring evidence. No descriptor installation, handler source, project default, wildcard, global grant, or ambient provider hook connects anything.
